extracted.intended_audience: readers of Popular Science Monthly — educated general public, scientists, students, and professionals seeking assessments of recent scientific and practical books
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria and standards used in short literary notices/reviews of scientific and practical books (assessment of usefulness, completeness, method, illustrations, and audience fit). Applies to reviews of popular-science, technical reports, and pedagogical works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical usefulness to intended readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the book will be helpful and serviceable to its intended audience (e.g., families, physicians, students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the cook-book 'can not fail to be helpful to families' and 'physicians may make it serviceable in providing a full dietary for their patients.' Assess whether content addresses everyday needs and professional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and usefulness of labeling/classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear labeling or classification of content to indicate suitability for specific sub-audiences (e.g., initials marking recipes for invalid, convalescent, dyspeptic, gouty, economical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: recipes marked (I, C, D, G, E) to guide different readers; evaluate whether such systems make the work more navigable and practically usable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity and practicality of instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the book provides concrete, specific procedures or methods that readers can follow (e.g., precise cooking directions, experimental methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a detailed warming method for meat, step-by-step experimental apparatus descriptions (weights, pins, smoked glass). Assess clarity, sufficiency of detail, and practicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and importance of introductory or explanatory essays
rubrics_metrics.description: Strength and relevance of introductory essays or prefatory material that situate the work in sanitary, scientific, historical, or methodological context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Fothergill's introduction is described as 'a very important and interesting essay on food in its sanitary relations.' Evaluate whether the introduction meaningfully frames the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological soundness and systematization
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the work provides a methodical, systematic approach appropriate to the subject (e.g., guides for data collection, schedules, or methods chapters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Powell's guide 'designed to aid in the collection of data' and to 'direct efforts methodically' with schedules; Cossa's treatment of method and discussion of methodological controversies. Evaluate presence of clear methods, schedules, blanks for notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical tools and instruments provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of usable instruments — alphabets, schedules, blanks, charts, or maps — that facilitate the reader's work or data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Powell's prepared alphabet and blanks for notes; Dutton's atlas and maps. Assess whether such tools are complete, usable, and well-integrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability and standardization of notation/transcription
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether proposed alphabets or notation allow representation of relevant sounds or data without requiring obscure symbols, and are practical for printing/use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Powell's alphabet 'seems to admit of the representation of all the sounds... without demanding the use of odd signs.' Evaluate practicality and adoptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and relevance of contextual/cultural material
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the work connects linguistic, historical, or ethnographic context (manners, customs, dress) to its main subject to illuminate data or interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Powell devotes a chapter to manners, customs, kinship charts which 'may throw light upon the main subject.' Assess relevance and integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness and breadth of coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which the work surveys its field, treats topics thoroughly, or provides wide-ranging lists/reviews (e.g., literature lists, historical reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cossa's 'long list' of writings with indications of worth; Darwin's work described as 'wellnigh exhaustive' for its subject. Evaluate depth and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and trustworthiness of scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability and competence of the author's treatment, informed by wide acquaintance with the literature and sound critical judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Cossa 'peculiarly fitted' by wide acquaintance to be a trustworthy guide. Assess accuracy, fairness, and scholarly competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrations and visual aids to clarify detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of plates, woodcuts, maps, atlases, diagrams, and photographic material that meaningfully clarify textual details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Dutton's atlas with topographical and geological maps; Darwin's woodcuts and diagrams showing circumnutation. Note completeness (e.g., photographic work unfinished) and whether illustrations serve the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental rigor and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: For experimental works, degree of rigor in experimental design, measurement, and apparatus, and the care of observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Darwin's use of tiny weights, smoked glass traces, measuring circumnutation; description of apparatus and quantitative methods. Assess repeatability and precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and novelty of contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the work contains fresh, original observations, methods, or interpretations that advance understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Darwin's 'no abatement of his power of work or his habits of fresh and original observation.' Evaluate novelty and contribution to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative and theoretical significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which the work connects specific findings to broader theory or comparative frameworks (e.g., linking plant movements to animal nervous systems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Darwin's analogy between plant movements and actions in animals, and implications for biological theory. Assess depth of theoretical insight and potential to stimulate further research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and chapter structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Logical organization of material into chapters/sections that address important topics and facilitate reader navigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Darwin devotes chapters to movement measurement, sensitiveness to light, sleep of plants; Cossa's division into general part and historical review. Evaluate coherence and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency and updating of facts
rubrics_metrics.description: How up-to-date the information is and whether facts are brought down to a recent year (currency of data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Young Folks' Cyclopedia 'facts are brought down to 1880.' Assess whether content reflects current knowledge for its publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age-appropriateness and clarity of language
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitability of language, explanations, and illustrations to the target age or level (e.g., young readers vs specialists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Young Folks' Cyclopedia uses simple language and explains technical terms; pronunciations indicated approximately. Evaluate readability for intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and novelty of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether illustrations are chosen to be informative and novel rather than typical school-book images, enhancing interest and understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: preference given to illustrations showing restorations of classic scenes and famous buildings, excluding common school-book images. Assess distinctiveness and pedagogical value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision and quality of indices and bibliographic apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of indexes, author lists, and bibliographic references that aid scholarly use and further research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Cossa's index containing over seven hundred names; Smithson volume includes reviews of scientific papers. Evaluate completeness and utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of limited or fragmentary source material
rubrics_metrics.description: How the author/editor deals with scanty, destroyed, or fragmentary original materials in producing biographical or documentary works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Smithson biography delayed by 'scantiness of the materials' and notes destroyed in a fire; assess transparency about sources and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of accompanying visual or photographic work
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether promised photographic or illustrative components are completed and included, affecting the work's completeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Dutton's photographic work 'not completed' and thus not embodied in the volume; evaluate whether missing components materially reduce value.
